QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_2

question.text: Lotus India AIF's compliance officer, Mr. Ramesh Iyer, must submit the fund's ACTIVITY REPORT to SEBI through the Intermediary Portal. Under the prevailing SEBI reporting framework, the filing deadline is:

answer.text: Within 15 calendar days from the end of each month
Within 30 calendar days from the end of each quarter
Within 7 working days from the end of each quarter
Within 10 calendar days from the end of each quarter

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular dated 07-Apr-2021 and Regulation 28, every AIF must file its quarterly activity report on the SEBI Intermediary Portal within 10 CALENDAR days from end of the quarter. Cat III funds file an additional leverage report in the same window. The Trap: 30 days conflates with the CTR sponsor-review period. 7 working days is the compliance-officer's deviation-reporting window to SEBI — a different regulation. Monthly filing does not exist for AIF activity reports. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) exams test this 10-day rule directly. XIX-A/B focus on investor-side disclosures rather than SEBI filings. XXI-B (PM) mandates monthly APMI reporting — a different regime. Manager's Pro-Tip: Treat T+10 as hard — SEBI's portal auto-flags delays and your fund's name surfaces in the next inspection letter. Keep a pre-populated template with the prior-quarter's portfolio so you only update deltas on day 1 of the new quarter.
